# 2 Kings Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 229v–231r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_009_page_001.jpg, 2KI_009_page_002.jpg, 2KI_009_page_003.jpg, 2KI_009_page_004.jpg

---

**1** Meanwhile, Elisha the prophet summoned one of the young prophets and said, "Get ready for a journey. Take this flask of oil and go to Ramoth-gilead.

**2** When you get there, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, grandson of Nimshi. Pull him away from his fellow officers and take him to a private room.

**3** Then pour this oil on his head and say, 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.' After that, open the door and run — don't wait around."

**4** So the young prophet headed for Ramoth-gilead.

**5** When he arrived, the army commanders were sitting together. "I have a message for you, commander," he said. "Which one of us?" Jehu asked. "For you, sir," the prophet replied.

**6** Jehu got up and went inside, and the young man poured oil on his head and said, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I anoint you king over the LORD's people Israel.

**7** You are to destroy the house of Ahab your master. I will avenge the blood of my prophets and all my servants who were murdered by Jezebel.

**8** The entire house of Ahab will be wiped out. I will cut off every last male in Ahab's line, slave and free alike, in Israel.

**9** I will make Ahab's dynasty like the dynasty of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the dynasty of Baasha son of Ahijah.

**10** As for Jezebel — the dogs will devour her on the plot of land at Jezreel, and no one will bury her.'" Then the young prophet flung open the door and ran.

**11** When Jehu came back out to his fellow officers, one of them asked, "Everything all right? What did that madman want with you?" "Oh, you know how those types talk," Jehu said evasively.

**12** "Come on, tell us!" they pressed. So he told them: "He said to me, 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.'"

**13** Instantly, every officer grabbed his cloak and spread it on the bare steps under Jehu. They blew the ram's horn and shouted, "Jehu is king!"

**14** So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, grandson of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been defending Ramoth-gilead against King Hazael of Aram with the whole Israelite army,

**15** but King Joram himself had gone back to Jezreel to recover from wounds the Arameans had given him in battle. Jehu said, "If you're with me, don't let anyone slip out of the city to warn Jezreel."

**16** Then Jehu got in his chariot and drove toward Jezreel, where Joram was recuperating. King Ahaziah of Judah had also come down to visit Joram.

**17** The watchman on the tower at Jezreel spotted Jehu's troops approaching. "I see a company of men!" he called out. Joram ordered, "Send a horseman to meet them and ask if they come in peace."

**18** The horseman rode out and said, "The king asks: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu shot back, "What do you know about peace? Fall in behind me." The watchman reported, "The messenger reached them but isn't coming back."

**19** A second horseman was sent with the same question: "Is it peace?" Jehu answered, "What do you know about peace? Fall in behind me."

**20** The watchman reported, "He reached them but isn't coming back either. And the lead driver — he drives like Jehu son of Nimshi. Like a lunatic!"

**21** "Get my chariot ready!" Joram ordered. His chariot was harnessed, and King Joram of Israel and King Ahaziah of Judah rode out, each in his own chariot, to meet Jehu. They met him at the plot of land that had belonged to Naboth of Jezreel.

**22** When Joram saw Jehu, he called out, "Is it peace, Jehu?" Jehu thundered back, "How can there be peace as long as the prostitution and witchcraft of your mother Jezebel run rampant?"

**23** Joram wheeled his chariot around and fled, shouting to Ahaziah, "It's a trap, Ahaziah!"

**24** But Jehu drew his bow with full force and shot Joram between the shoulder blades. The arrow pierced his heart, and he slumped dead in his chariot.

**25** Jehu told his officer Bidkar, "Pick him up and throw him on the field that belonged to Naboth of Jezreel. Remember? You and I were riding behind his father Ahab when the LORD pronounced this judgment against him:

**26** 'I saw the blood of Naboth and his sons yesterday, declares the LORD, and I will make you pay for it on this very plot of ground, declares the LORD.' Now throw him on that land, just as the LORD said."

**27** When King Ahaziah of Judah saw what happened, he fled toward Beth-haggan. Jehu pursued him, shouting, "Get him too!" They wounded him in his chariot at the pass of Gur near Ibleam. He managed to escape to Megiddo, but he died there.

**28** His servants brought his body back to Jerusalem in a chariot and buried him in his tomb with his ancestors in the City of David.

**29** Ahaziah had begun his reign over Judah in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab.

**30** When Jehu arrived in Jezreel, Jezebel got the news. She painted her eyes, styled her hair, and positioned herself at an upper window.

**31** As Jehu rode through the gate, she called down, "Did you come in peace, Zimri — you who murdered your master?"

**32** Jehu looked up at the window and shouted, "Who's on my side? Who?" Two or three palace eunuchs peered down at him.

**33** "Throw her down!" he ordered. They threw her out the window. Her blood splashed against the wall and the horses, and Jehu rode over her body.

**34** He went inside, sat down, and had a meal. Then he said, "Go deal with that cursed woman — give her a proper burial. After all, she was a king's daughter."

**35** But when they went to bury her, all they found was her skull, her feet, and her hands.

**36** They came back and told Jehu, and he said, "This is exactly what the LORD said through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'On the plot of ground at Jezreel, dogs will devour Jezebel's flesh.

**37** Her remains will be scattered like manure on the ground at Jezreel, so that no one will ever be able to say, Here lies Jezebel.'"

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 3 — "open the door and run":** Elisha sends a young prophet rather than going himself — and tells him to flee immediately after the anointing. The speed and secrecy are essential: this is a military coup disguised as a prophetic commission. The young man is literally lighting a fuse and running.

**Verse 11 — "that madman":** The Hebrew *meshugga'* was commonly applied to ecstatic prophets. The officers' casual dismissal — and Jehu's cagey deflection ("you know how those types talk") — captures the uneasy relationship between military men and prophets. When Jehu finally reveals the message, the officers' instant, wholehearted response shows they were ready for revolution.

**Verse 20 — "he drives like a lunatic":** Jehu's driving is so reckless it serves as an identity marker — the ancient equivalent of a police profile. The Hebrew *shigga'on* (madness/frenzy) deliberately echoes the *meshugga'* label from v.11. This chapter is driven (literally) by a particular kind of furious energy.

**Verse 22 — The *shalom* refrain:** The word "peace" (*shalom*) is asked five times in this chapter (vv.17, 18, 19, 22, 31), and each time the answer pushes further from peace. Jehu's devastating reply — "How can there be peace while your mother's prostitution and witchcraft run rampant?" — transforms a diplomatic greeting into a theological indictment.

**Verse 30-31 — Jezebel's final act:** Jezebel does not cower. She paints her eyes (a mark of royal dignity, not seduction), styles her hair (queenly authority), positions herself at the window (the seat of power), and delivers a cutting historical insult. "Zimri" lasted seven days as king before dying. Her message: you'll end the same way. She dies as she lived — defiant, regal, and wielding words like blades.

**Verse 37 — The erasure:** The most devastating punishment in the ancient world was not death but the obliteration of memory. No tomb, no marker, no remains anyone could identify. Jezebel's body becomes fertilizer. Her name — which once commanded kingdoms — becomes a cautionary tale with no grave to visit.

*— PNEUMA*
